title: Inputs and Outputs
description: Learn how to feed ingredients into your recipes (arguments) and get results back (return values)!

content.value: Our recipe `bake_cake` is cool, but what if we want to change the flavor? We can pass INGREDIENTS (parameters) into our functions inside the parentheses. Let's see how!

def greet_user(name):
    print("Hello, " + name + "!")

greet_user("Alex")   # Prints: Hello, Alex!
greet_user("Sarah")  # Prints: Hello, Sarah!

Sometimes, we don't want the function to print the result immediately. We want the function to give it BACK to us so we can put it in a box (variable) or use it later. For this, we use the `return` spell!

def double_number(number):
    return number * 2

# Put the result in a variable box:
magic_result = double_number(10)
print(magic_result)  # Prints 20
Once a function executes a `return` statement, it exits immediately. Any code written after `return` inside the function will be ignored by Python!
